newsitem.title: CYPRUS: SOCCER-CYPRUS, ISRAEL TEAMS CONFIDENT OF WIN IN MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CYPRUS, ISRAEL TEAMS CONFIDENT OF WIN IN MATCH.

text.p: Team coaches of the Israeli and Cypriot national teams playing in Sunday's World Cup qualifier in Limassol declared confidence of a win on Friday, despite injuries on both sides.

"We are sure they will be a tough opponent for us but we are here to win this match to keep up our fine run in the preliminary round of the World Cup," Israeli coach Sholomon Sharf told a news conference.
Sharf said the team had to work hard to get three points to knock Russia off the top of the group 5 table. "There are no easy matches anymore," he said.
The match will be held at Limassol's Tsirion stadium on Sunday at 6.00 p.m. local time (1600 GMT).
Cypriot coach Andreas Michaelides was equally confident of a win. "We were unbeaten at the last official matches at home. Our aim is to keep this record and I am sure we can do it," he said.
On Friday Michaelides pulled out defender George Theodotou and midfielder Neophytos Larkou, both for leg injuries. They were replaced by Angelos Misos and Aristos Aristotelous.
The participation of forward Yiotis Engomitis, also suffering an injury, is questionable, team officials said.
Earlier this week Sharf recalled right back Moshe Glam to cover for injured midfielder David Amsalem.
Five of Israel's 20-man squad are carrying leg injuries into the group five match with Amsalem and captain Ronnen Harazi doubtful starters.
Glam has not played for Israel since the start of the World Cup qualifying campaign and has hardly played for his club, Maccabi Haifa, while awaiting a transfer to another side.
Harazi has been out of action since Israel's last qualifying match against Russia in Tel Aviv last month.
